summary:
Yesterday I received an email with the subject “Rp2350 pi pico 2 modified one”.  I found the request funny because it features an illustration with a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 board and an Apple Lightning cable, and I had no idea why somebody would do that at the time. Coming to my physical address (today!) was also humorous considering where I live… Nevertheless, I decided to share the screenshot above on X, and quickly found out the reasons: jailbreaking/bypassing iDevices with Apple A12/A13 CPUs using the usbliter8 boot ROM exploit by Paradigm Shift. title: Quectel SH602FA and SE505FE smart modules bring Android 16 to 4G LTE and 5G IoT devices
summary:
Quectel has just introduced the SH602FA 4G LTE Cat 4 and SE505FE 5G Sub-6 GHz Android 16-smart IoT modules. Both integrate octa-core MediaTek processors, cellular connectivity, wireless interfaces, and multimedia functions for devices such as smart displays, point-of-sale terminals, industrial handhelds, and robots. The “high-performance” 4G LTE SH602FA module is built around the MediaTek MT8786 Cortex-A75/A55 processor, while the “entry-level” 5G SE505FE module is powered by a MediaTek MT8863T Cortex-A76/A55 SoC. Both modules are available in multiple regional variants, as well as a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth-only “-WF” variant. summary:

Pine64 started with the launch of the Pine A64 development board in 2015, and since then they have launched more Arm and RISC-V Linux SBCs, Linux smartphones, and Linux tablets and e-Readers. We used to get several announcements per year, but this year so far, we only covered one: the Pine64 PineVoice. But it’s not a Linux device, and instead, a smart speaker based on a BL602 RISC-V microcontroller. Here’s the full (unedited) announcement published on Telegram, which you should also find on other Pine64 channels: Hi everyone! It targets industrial and networking applications such as controllers, PLCs, remote I/O, building and energy management systems, and other connected edge devices. title: USBridge-KVM 2.0 – An open-source IP-KVM with BIOS access over SSH, OCR, and AI support (Crowdfunding)
summary:
USBridge-KVM 2.0 is a compact open-source AI-enabled IP-KVM designed for remote management and troubleshooting of servers and PCs, including systems that are unresponsive or have not yet booted. It provides out-of-band BIOS access, remote display and input control, virtual media mounting, and hardware power management. Built around a Radxa Zero 3W single board computer, it also features a 240×240 IPS display, Wi-Fi 6 connectivity, two USB Type-C ports, a Micro HDMI video output (loop), and a MicroSD card slot. It supports hardware UVC video capture up to 1080p and uses Moonlight streaming to achieve 25–50 ms low-latency remote access. One of the most notable features is the BIOS-in-Terminal, which uses offline OCR to convert BIOS and pre-boot screens into text accessible over SSH. USBridge-KVM 2.0 specifications: Main SBC – Radxa Zero 3W with Rockchip RK3566, 1-2GB LPDDR4X RAM, and MicroSD storage for the OS and Btrfs snapshots Display – 240×240 IPS [...]

title: SONOFF Hydro DUO review – A dual-zone BLE and Zigbee water valve tested with eWeLink and Home Assistant
summary:
ITEAD has sent us a review sample of the SONOFF Hydro DUO (SWV-ZF2E) dual-channel Zigbee 3.0 and Bluetooth 5 LE smart water valve. The device supports up to 12 custom watering schedules, integrates a water flow meter, and features alert systems for leak risks, low battery, and insufficient water. The device has a maximum Zigbee communication range of 130 meters in open, unobstructed areas. It is primarily designed for the eWeLink app but also works with MQTT-compatible platforms such as Home Assistant. In this review, we will cover everything from unboxing, installation, and getting started with the SONOFF Hydro DUO via Bluetooth LE and Zigbee (through the SONOFF NSPanel Pro Gen2) using the eWeLink app, before switching to Home Assistant and creating an automation system leveraging moisture data from the XIAO Soil Moisture Sensor.
